name: Client Brief — Household-Wide Roles Question Declined and Handed Off
query: Who's the successor trustee for the Bradys?
context: Advisor has already been given the orientation brief for Robert and Susan Brady (CA) in this session.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Recognises this as a household-wide roles question, not a question about one named document
Step 2: Makes no tool call — there is no household-level roles read available today
Step 3: Does not fall back to Wealth:get_flowchart, Wealth:get_estate_roles, or Wealth:get_estate_flow
Step 4: States plainly that this is answered per document, not for the household as a whole
Step 5: Offers the real documents on file by name (the joint revocable trust, the family ILIT) as the way to proceed
Step 6: On the advisor naming one, stops and hands off — does not attempt to answer the roles question itself
success_criteria: Zero tool calls in this turn
The decline names at least one real document from the earlier list_documents result
Exactly one offer, phrased as a question
The handoff turn (after a document is named) contains no roles content of its own
must_not: any call to get_flowchart, get_estate_roles, or get_estate_flow
a rolled-up household roles answer assembled from anything already in context
presenting a household-level answer as if get_flowchart's per-node role field still applies at that scope
the phrase 'I don't have that' without offering the document-level path forward
estate flow, at-death, insights, or risk analysis anywhere in the answer
notes: This gate has no numeric ID in the RFC's risk register because it's a tools-reconciliation finding, not an original design risk — get_flowchart's (formerly get_estate_snapshot's) role field was briefly assumed to cover this at the household level, and doesn't; get_flowchart requiring a vaultId confirms it structurally can't. If a household-level roles tool ever ships, this eval gets rewritten to a real happy path, not deleted.
